title: A Crown for the Salt
premise: Edmund Ravensworth, a mercenary whose god fell silent two decades ago, survives by selling illegal charms in the salt-locked city of Greyharbor. When a dying courier presses a map into his hands — a map to the drowned vault where that god's heart still beats — Edmund becomes hunted by both the city's witch-hunters and the cult that silenced the divine. Carrying the map means choosing between a safe small life and reigniting an ancient war between gods and men. In the end, Edmund reaches the vault and discovers the god was never silent but imprisoned, and he must decide whether to free it: he shatters the seal, accepts exile from Greyharbor, and walks into a changed world where magic — and belonging — must be rebuilt from salt and ash.
about_author: Paloma Amberdale is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent years cataloguing shipwreck salvage before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about people who survive at the edges of empires, drawing on coastal folklore and her collection of half-legible sea charts.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller's Hour
chapters.summary: Edmund sells a luck-charm to a dockworker's widow while hiding the tremor of dead magic in his hands. His POV establishes Greyharbor's anti-magic laws, his quiet shame, and the ritual prayers he still whispers to a silent god. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as routine.

chapters.title: Salt on the Doorstep
chapters.summary: A dying stranger collapses in Edmund's stairwell, bleeding from a wound that burns like holy fire. With his last breath the man presses a wax-sealed map into Edmund's hands and says the god's true name. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: terror — the past has found him.

chapters.title: What the Tide Refuses
chapters.summary: Edmund tries to burn the map; the parchment refuses flame. He recognizes the cartography as pre-Silencing work, drawn by hands like his own. Flashback to his mercenary days and the night every god went quiet. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: grief resurfacing after twenty frozen years.

chapters.title: The Witch-Hunter's Courtesy
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Serah Vole pays a polite, menacing visit, having traced the dying stranger's route to Edmund's door. She offers protection in exchange for the map. Edmund lies for the first time in years. POV alternates: Edmund, then Vole's cold certainty. Emotional beat: the noose tightening gently.

chapters.title: Nine Bells for the Drowned
chapters.summary: Edmund seeks out Maren Quill, an old smuggler who once crewed with him, hoping she can read the map's tide-marks. She agrees — for a share of whatever it leads to. POV: Maren, revealing Edmund through old eyes. Emotional beat: wary rekindled trust.

chapters.title: A Debt Paid in Iron
chapters.summary: Cultists of the Hollow Choir attack Edmund's shop, seeking the map. He kills for the first time since his mercenary days and realizes his dormant magic flared to save him. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: horror at what survival costs him.

chapters.title: The Choir That Sings Silence
chapters.summary: Vole interrogates a captured cultist and learns the Hollow Choir imprisoned the gods deliberately, believing silence saved mankind. Her faith begins to crack. POV: Vole. Emotional beat: doubt planted in a true believer.

chapters.title: Downriver, Running
chapters.summary: Edmund and Maren flee Greyharbor by night aboard a coal barge, pursued by both hunters and Choir. On the water, Edmund admits the god's name aloud for the first time. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: exhilaration tangled with dread — he is becoming himself again.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Toll
chapters.summary: At the river-town of Brackwater they need passage upstream; the ferryman demands a memory as payment. Edmund surrenders his wedding day — a marriage Maren never knew about. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: love and loss measured in what can't be bought back.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Vigil
chapters.summary: They shelter with a hidden congregation of god-sworn survivors who have kept vigil for twenty years. Their hope terrifies Edmund: they think he's a herald. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: the crushing weight of other people's faith.

chapters.title: Vole Descends
chapters.summary: Vole tracks them to the congregation and finds burned children among the vigil-keepers — the Choir arrived first. She saves a survivor instead of arresting Edmund, and defects in all but name. POV: Vole. Emotional beat: allegiance breaking like ice.

chapters.title: The Map's Second Face
chapters.summary: Maren discovers the map shows two destinations: the drowned vault, and a Choir stronghold where something is kept caged. They realize the god's heart is split — or guarded twice. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: the plan grows teeth.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Salt Road
chapters.summary: Crossing the salt flats, the party is ambushed by Choir knights. Edmund's magic erupts uncontrollably, saving them but scarring Maren. She forgives him — barely. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: power as something that wounds what it protects.

chapters.title: The Caged Bell
chapters.summary: Infiltrating the Choir stronghold, they find not half a heart but a living priest — the man who cast the Silencing spell, kept alive as the seal's anchor. He begs them to let him die and end it. POV: Vole. Emotional beat: mercy versus necessity.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: The anchor-priest tells the truth: the gods chose silence willingly to stop a war, and the Choir merely locked the door behind them. Freeing the god may unleash what silence contained. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: the mission's moral floor gives way.

chapters.title: Maren's Choice
chapters.summary: Maren reveals she has known the truth for years — her brother helped build the seal — and joined Edmund to reach the vault first and destroy it forever. Knife-point standoff. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: betrayal inside loyalty.

chapters.title: The Drowned Vault
chapters.summary: Reconciled but shaken, the three descend into the flooded vault beneath the sea-cliffs, where the god's heart beats in the dark like a second tide. The Choir arrives above. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: awe before the divine, finally face to face.

chapters.title: An Audience of One
chapters.summary: The god speaks to Edmund alone — not in command but in question: do you belong to me, or yourself? It offers him everything he lost. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: identity tested against longing.

chapters.title: The Breaking of the Seal
chapters.summary: Choir forces breach the vault; Vole holds the line and falls buying time. Edmund, choosing neither servitude nor silence, shatters the seal on his own terms — freeing the god without kneeling. POV: Vole, then Edmund. Emotional beat: sacrifice crowned with defiance.

chapters.title: When the Gods Woke
chapters.summary: Magic floods back into the world; Greyharbor's laws collapse overnight as charms ignite across the city. The awakened god does not make war — it asks. But some Choir remnants refuse peace. POV: multiple brief vignettes. Emotional beat: the world remade, uncertain and bright.

chapters.title: Exile's Harbor
chapters.summary: Edmund returns to Greyharbor in disguise, frees Maren from the mob justice awaiting her, and together they slip out of the city that outlawed them both. He buries the map at sea. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: grief and release entwined.

chapters.title: A Crown for the Salt
chapters.summary: On a northern shore, Edmund builds a school for the newly magic-born, teaching them that power needs no crown. The god visits sometimes, quietly, as an equal. POV: Edmund, closing letter to Vole's memory. Emotional beat: belonging finally earned, not granted.
